content.synthesis_comparative_analysis:
**Three-axis comparison of Miles' funding posture vs. adjacent peers at Iowa**:

| Dimension | David Miles (lead-013) | Craig Kletzing (Miles' mentor, formerly TRACERS PI per Kletzing grants page) | Jasper Halekas (TRACERS ACES PI; contact for Req. 75971) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mission-level funding as PI | Yes — TRACERS PI from Sept 2023 (mission cost cap $115M) | Was TRACERS PI; still listed as PI/award-recipient on [synthesis_comparative_analysis[0]] [46] | TRACERS ACE instrument PI per [synthesis_comparative_analysis[1]] [45] |
| 2024-2026 NASA competitive grant | Co-investigator on $1.495M NASA SSMS award (DeRoo PI) | (No new 2024-2026 award verified in this run) | Co-investigator on same $1.495M SSMS award |
| Open departmental faculty hire | None attributed to Miles; Req. 75971 contact is Halekas | None verified | Listed as contact for Req. 75971 |
| Mechanisms | Mission lead (TRACERS) + equipment co-investigator; hires through internal lab growth | Held TRACERS PI role until Sept 2023 | Magnetic reconnection instrument PI |
| Trade-off: mission vs. personal grant | TRACERS dominates Miles' funding narrative; competitive personal grants are smaller and as co-I | TRACERS institutional lineage pre-Sept 2023 | TRACERS instrument-level PI; co-I on 2024 hardware award |
| Time horizon | Mission active through end of 2026+; postdoc cohort size implies continued flow | Long-running mission tenure | Continuing instrument PI role |

**Tensions and divergences**:
1. **PI transition timing**: Kletzing's grants page still lists TRACERS under his name with $115M; Iowa announced Miles as PI in Sept 2023. Both pages are consistent if Miles is the science PI going forward and Kletzing remains the institutional award owner until contract novation. Researchers verifying funding should note this dual-listing.
2. **Lab scale vs. personal-grant funding**: Miles' group supports 3 postdocs, 4 engineers and 2 graduate teaching assistants. The publicly documented competitive grant dollar amount attributable to Miles specifically (as PI/co-I in 2024-2026) is $1.495M as co-I, far smaller than what is needed to fund such a group, implying that TRACERS mission subcontracts and ISL internal funds carry the bulk of staff costs. This is consistent with TRACERS being the dominant funding vector.
3. **Hiring pipeline**: Open departmental faculty hire (Req. 75971) does not name Miles; the Miles lab currently lacks an advertised Miles-line open postdoc or PhD posting. A lead interested in joining Miles' group should contact Miles directly ([david-miles@uiowa.edu](mailto:david-miles@uiowa.edu)) or apply through general Iowa Physics graduate admissions, not through a dedicated lab posting.
4. **Recommendation**: pursue Miles as a TRACERS-aligned PI rather than as a personal competitive-grant PI. Hard-money TRACERS subcontract coverage and ISL postdoc lines are the channel; an explicit Miles-line NSF or fellowship award is not in evidence from this research.
